text: The $\textbf{2000 Summer Olympics}$ were held in $\textbf{Sydney}$, the most populous city in $\textbf{Australia}$, showcasing the iconic Opera House and Harbour Bridge.
explanation: It was the second time Australia hosted the Olympics, the first being Melbourne in 1956.

text: The $\textbf{Oresund Bridge}$ opened in 2000, creating a direct rail and road link between $\textbf{Copenhagen}$, Denmark, and $\textbf{Malmö}$, $\textbf{Sweden}$.
explanation: The bridge spans the Oresund strait and created a combined metropolitan region known as the Oresund Region.

text: On December 31, 1999, just hours before 2000 began, the $\textbf{Panama Canal}$ was fully transferred from the $\textbf{United States}$ to $\textbf{Panama}$.
explanation: This ended nearly a century of American jurisdiction over the strategic waterway.

text: The $\textbf{International Space Station}$ (ISS) received its first long-term resident crew (Expedition 1) in 2000, orbiting 400 km above the $\textbf{Earth}$.
explanation: This marked the beginning of uninterrupted human presence in low Earth orbit.

text: The $\textbf{Kursk}$ submarine disaster occurred in the $\textbf{Barents Sea}$ off the coast of $\textbf{Russia}$ in August 2000.
explanation: The tragedy involved the loss of all 118 personnel on board during a naval exercise.

text: The $\textbf{London Eye}$, a giant observation wheel on the South Bank of the $\textbf{River Thames}$, officially opened to the public in March 2000.
explanation: It was built to celebrate the new millennium and offers panoramic views of London.

text: Devastating floods struck $\textbf{Mozambique}$ in 2000, caused by a cyclone and rising levels in the $\textbf{Limpopo River}$.
explanation: The floods displaced hundreds of thousands and highlighted the vulnerability of the region to climate extremes.

text: The $\textbf{USS Cole}$ was bombed by terrorists while refueling in the port of $\textbf{Aden}$ in $\textbf{Yemen}$.
explanation: Aden is a strategic port city located near the entrance to the Red Sea.

text: Mount $\textbf{Usu}$ in $\textbf{Hokkaido}$, $\textbf{Japan}$, erupted in 2000, forcing the evacuation of thousands of residents and tourists.
explanation: Japan sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire and frequently experiences volcanic activity.

text: The $\textbf{Tate Modern}$ art gallery opened in 2000, housed in the former Bankside Power Station in $\textbf{London}$.
explanation: It became one of the most visited modern art galleries in the world.

text: Israel withdrew its troops from southern $\textbf{Lebanon}$ in 2000, ending an 18-year occupation of the security zone.
explanation: The withdrawal was certified by the UN, establishing the 'Blue Line' boundary.

text: The $\textbf{Millennium Dome}$ (now The O2) was built on the Greenwich Peninsula in London, located precisely on the $\textbf{Prime Meridian}$.
explanation: It was constructed to house a major exhibition celebrating the beginning of the third millennium.

text: The $\textbf{Chernobyl}$ nuclear power plant in $\textbf{Ukraine}$ was permanently shut down in 2000 with the closure of the last reactor.
explanation: The plant had continued to operate partially for years after the 1986 disaster.

text: The $\textbf{Second Intifada}$ began in late 2000, intensifying conflict in the $\textbf{West Bank}$ and $\textbf{Gaza Strip}$.
explanation: The uprising was triggered after a controversial visit to the Temple Mount in Jerusalem.

text: Vicente Fox was elected president of $\textbf{Mexico}$ in 2000, ending 71 years of rule by the $\textbf{PRI}$ party.
explanation: It was a landmark event in the democratization of Latin America's second-largest economy.

text: The $\textbf{Concorde}$ supersonic jet crashed in Gonesse, $\textbf{France}$, shortly after takeoff from Paris in July 2000.
explanation: The tragedy marked the beginning of the end for commercial supersonic flight.

text: The $\textbf{Eritrea-Ethiopia War}$ concluded in 2000 with the Algiers Agreement, settling the border dispute in the $\textbf{Horn of Africa}$.
explanation: The war was fought over the border town of Badme.

text: The $\textbf{Belgrade}$ protests in 2000 led to the resignation of Slobodan Milošević, ending his rule over the Federal Republic of $\textbf{Yugoslavia}$.
explanation: The 'Bulldozer Revolution' paved the way for democratic transition in Serbia.

text: The $\textbf{Hekla}$ volcano in $\textbf{Iceland}$, often called the 'Gateway to Hell', erupted in February 2000.
explanation: It is one of Iceland's most active volcanoes.

text: The $\textbf{US Census 2000}$ confirmed a population shift toward the $\textbf{South}$ and $\textbf{West}$ regions of the country.
explanation: States like Nevada, Arizona, and Georgia saw massive growth.

text: British forces intervened in $\textbf{Sierra Leone}$ in 2000 (Operation Palliser) to support the government during the civil war.
explanation: The intervention helped secure the capital, Freetown, and bring an end to the conflict.

text: The $\textbf{Hafez al-Assad}$ era ended in $\textbf{Syria}$ in 2000 with his death, leading to the succession of his son, Bashar al-Assad.
explanation: This transition of power maintained the Ba'ath Party's control over the country.

text: The $\textbf{Maasvlakte}$ extension of the Port of $\textbf{Rotterdam}$ in the $\textbf{Netherlands}$ continued to be a major engineering project in 2000.
explanation: Rotterdam was the world's busiest port at the time (by tonnage).

text: The $\textbf{Plan Colombia}$ was initiated in 2000, a US-funded aid plan aimed at combating drug cartels in $\textbf{Colombia}$.
explanation: The plan focused on the cultivation of coca and the conflict with FARC rebels.

text: The $\textbf{Three Gorges Dam}$ construction in $\textbf{China}$ required the forced relocation of over 1 million people along the $\textbf{Yangtze River}$.
explanation: By 2000, the dam was heavily under construction, transforming the geography of the region.

text: The $\textbf{Great Barrier Reef}$ suffered a significant bleaching event, raising early alarms about ocean warming off the coast of $\textbf{Australia}$.
explanation: Coral bleaching is caused by thermal stress, expelling the symbiotic algae.

text: The $\textbf{Amazon Rainforest}$ deforestation rate in $\textbf{Brazil}$ remained a critical global environmental issue in 2000.
explanation: The Amazon is the world's largest tropical rainforest and a vital carbon sink.

text: The $\textbf{Antarctic Ozone Hole}$ reached a record size of 29.9 million square kilometers in September 2000.
explanation: The hole forms annually over the South Pole due to CFCs and unique atmospheric conditions.

text: The $\textbf{Diavik Diamond Mine}$ began construction in 2000 in the remote Northwest Territories of $\textbf{Canada}$.
explanation: Located on an island in Lac de Gras, it is accessible by an ice road in winter.

text: Chen Shui-bian was elected president of $\textbf{Taiwan}$ in 2000, ending more than 50 years of KMT rule on the island.
explanation: This marked the first democratic transfer of power between parties in Taiwan's history.

text: The $\textbf{Resurgent Russia}$ under Vladimir Putin, elected in 2000, began consolidating power and dealing with the conflict in $\textbf{Chechnya}$.
explanation: The Second Chechen War was a major focus of Putin's early presidency.

text: The $\textbf{Aral Sea}$ continued its rapid shrinkage in 2000, splitting into North and South Aral Seas between $\textbf{Kazakhstan}$ and Uzbekistan.
explanation: Once the fourth largest lake, it is a symbol of environmental mismanagement.

text: The $\textbf{Euro}$ existed as an accounting currency in 2000, with the $\textbf{European Central Bank}$ located in $\textbf{Frankfurt}$, Germany.
explanation: The ECB sets monetary policy for the Eurozone.

text: The $\textbf{Millau Viaduct}$, planned to be the tallest bridge in the world, was in the early construction phases in $\textbf{France}$ in 2000.
explanation: It spans the valley of the River Tarn near Millau.

text: The $\textbf{Camp David Summit}$ in 2000 attempted to negotiate a final status agreement between $\textbf{Israel}$ and the $\textbf{Palestinian Authority}$.
explanation: The failure of the summit was a precursor to the Second Intifada.

text: The $\textbf{Kilauea}$ volcano in $\textbf{Hawaii}$ continued its long-term eruption in 2000, adding new land to the Big Island.
explanation: It is one of the most active volcanoes on Earth.

text: The $\textbf{Mekong River}$ Commission continued efforts in 2000 to manage shared water resources in $\textbf{Southeast Asia}$.
explanation: The river flows through China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, and Vietnam.

text: The $\textbf{Bosphorus Bridge}$ in $\textbf{Istanbul}$ is a vital link between Europe and Asia, crossing the Bosphorus Strait.
explanation: Istanbul is the only major city located on two continents.

text: The $\textbf{Strait of Malacca}$ remained the world's busiest shipping lane in 2000, connecting the $\textbf{Indian Ocean}$ and the Pacific Ocean.
explanation: It is a critical chokepoint for global oil transport.

text: Political crisis in $\textbf{Peru}$ in 2000 led to the resignation of President Alberto Fujimori, who fled to $\textbf{Japan}$.
explanation: The crisis was triggered by corruption scandals involving intelligence chief Vladimiro Montesinos.
